title: Trade-based money laundering
definition: The use of the movement of goods and services — rather than of cash — to move value across a border, usually by over-invoicing or under-invoicing the trade, so that the value transferred and the value of the goods diverge. The defining feature is a divergence between a declared value and an independently supportable value, which requires a comparison class to be meaningful.
evidence_to_cite: the invoices, the contracts and the payments, each cited by its own source id
the independent evidence of market value relied on, and the comparison class used
the shipping, customs and insurance documentation for the goods
benign_explanations: Related parties priced on a cost-plus basis as a matter of group policy.
A market with few comparable trades, in which any benchmark is weak.
Freight, insurance and tax bundled into one invoice and excluded from the other.
A genuine change of price, quantity or quality between the compared periods.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, trade-based money laundering guidance, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.
